quantity: j_{m,s} : the s-th positive zero of the Bessel function J_m

anchor.citation: Abramowitz M. & Stegun I. A. (eds.), Handbook of Mathematical Functions with Formulas, Graphs, and Mathematical Tables, NBS Applied Mathematics Series 55, 1964 (10th printing, 1972), Chapter 9 'Bessel Functions of Integer Order', section 9.5 'Zeros', Table 9.5 'Zeros of Bessel Functions J_0(x), J_1(x), Y_0(x), Y_1(x)', printed pages 370-373
anchor.section_page_pin: section 9.5 starts on printed page 370 and runs to printed page 373 (verified 2026-11-13 against the table of contents of the electronic 10th printing: entry '9.5. Zeros 370 371 372 373', https://personal.math.ubc.ca/~cbm/aands/toc.htm)
anchor.coverage: Table 9.5 tabulates the zeros of J_0, J_1, Y_0, Y_1 only, i.e. the families j_{0,s} and j_{1,s}; higher integer orders are NOT in that table
anchor.higher_order_anchor: for m >= 2 the reference used here is the same constant computed to 40 digits by mpmath.besseljzero and independently by scipy.special.jn_zeros and by the numpy-only recurrence+bisection solver in tensorbem.benchmarks.irregular_frequency_study.dirichlet_zeros; those rows are marked source='computed' and are NOT claimed to be handbook readings
anchor.why_no_ocr: the electronic edition serves the pages of section 9.5 as page images (page_370.jpg .. page_373.jpg); no OCR engine is installed in this environment, so the printed digits could not be machine-read - recorded as ecosystem friction in the case report

audit_note: every literal is re-derived at run time by mpmath.besseljzero at 40 digits; a literal that misses by more than audit_tolerance_absolute aborts the case (transcription guard). 6e-11 is ~1.2 ULP of a 10-decimal literal, so correct rounding passes and a wrong digit cannot.
